## The paradox

_Eight reporters, each on their own beat. They read the same articles and tell you what they see — suggestion with citations, never proof of anyone's motive. When they split, the split is the story._

**Split.** hermes, hades, demeter pushed back; nemesis, dionysus checked out; janus, eros, persephone sat it out. Both readings stand — here is the whole split, nothing softened.

### Hermes — pushes back

_Beat: do the outlets' framings of the same event diverge, and what does the divergence hide?_

Same event, 9 outlets, 9 different front doors. Here is how each one leads it: PBS opens with "House Republicans adopt $95 billion package for the Iran war and Trump's priorities"; PBS opens with "Some House Republicans defect to again pass resolution seeking to halt military action in Iran"; Politico opens with "‘A circular firing squad’: Senate GOP pushes back on Trump’s tiff with Thune"; Roll Call opens with "GOP budget blueprint adopted in House as Senate resists".

I read every version, and they are barely the same story. PBS wants you thinking about "House Republicans adopt $95 billion package for the Iran war and Trump's priorities". PBS wants you thinking about "Some House Republicans defect to again pass resolution seeking to halt military action in ". Politico wants you thinking about "‘A circular firing squad’: Senate GOP pushes back on Trump’s tiff with Thune". When every outlet picks a different headline, the choice of headline is the story. Read one and you will feel informed. Read them all and you will realize each one buried somebody else's lead.

**Why Hermes reads it this way:** My beat is framing: how the outlets choose to tell the same event. I pulled the key names and terms from each of the 9 outlets' headlines and compared them — only 17% overlapped, and my bar for "the same story" is 60%. Concretely: PBS leads with "House Republicans adopt $95 billion package for the Iran war and Trump's priorities" while PBS leads with "Some House Republicans defect to again pass resolution seeking to halt military action in ". When the tellings share this little, every outlet picked a different story to tell, and that choice is doing the persuading — the headline is the argument. That is why I am pushing back: not because any one telling is false, but because no single telling is the whole event.

## In their own words

_The panel, in plain talk._

**Hermes:** PBS's headline is "House Republicans adopt $95 billion package for the Iran war and Trump's priorities." PBS's headline is "Some House Republicans defect to again pass resolution seeking to halt military action in Iran." Politico's headline is "‘A circular firing squad’: Senate GOP pushes back on Trump’s tiff with Thune." Roll Call's headline is "GOP budget blueprint adopted in House as Senate resists." Same event, 9 outlets, and they're not telling it the same way.

**Hades:** No direct quotes from anyone. A quote without a name isn't a source.

**Demeter:** spans 48 hours spans 48 hours. This doesn't go away when the news cycle moves on.

**Nemesis:** At least nobody's hiding here. The coverage names who's doing what. You might not like it, but they're not pretending someone else did it.

**Dionysus:** 9 outlets on this one and they're all reporting the same facts. That's unusual. The spin is in the headlines, not the facts.
